CHART OF THE DAY: What food crisis? 

Nine months into the war, the world is experiencing little food inflation (📉⤵️). The price of US wheat is even lower now than in late Feb. Corn and soybean are little changed. And fertiliezers? The infamous urea costs 10% less than pre-war. https://t.co/8kr51jNmXW

Iraq says it has re-started oil exports via its historic Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline after a 12-year hiatus (Ceyhan is a Turkish port in the Mediterranean Sea).

The line inside Iraqi territory was sabotaged in 2014. At the time, the Kurdistan regional government built a second line from its territory, linking to the original pipeline at the Iraq-Turkish border (in Faysh Khabur), allowing KRG oil exports while the rest of the line inside Iraqi territory remained out of service. 

Baghdad said the now re-activated Kirkuk-to-the Turkish border portion of the pipeline would pump at 120,000 b/d initially, with aim of raising that to 500,000 b/d at an undetermined future date.

BREAKING: Big disinflation news in America. 

The US average retail gasoline price has fallen this morning to a 8-month low ($3.7818 per gallon) as strong refining margins for diesel keep gasoline supply abundant just as demand seasonally drops (plus winter grade gasoline is cheaper to make).

Oil bears ascendant as Gulf exports accelerate

Investors have become very bearish about petroleum prices as increasing amounts of crude are exported from countries around the Persian Gulf despite the absence of a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran.

Fund managers have sold a total of 184 million barrels in just the last three weeks and 258 million barrels since the middle of September, according to position records published by regulators ...

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen
